## Final report (your last message)

Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.

For source-backed formalization, add a compact epistemic checkpoint to the same
report (it is not needed for an ordinary tooling task):
`Claim class: proved producer | conditional interface | imported boundary |
empty/vacuous | axiom/sorry-backed | unverified`; `Frontier before/after:` the
source-facing node and first unmet producer; `Consumer:` the intended downstream
declaration/node; and `Evidence:` the exact target/build, transitive `#print axioms`,
and source/graph status. State `honesty-reviewer: used` or `skipped — <reason>`
when a certificate, completion claim, or repeated frontier triggered the lane.
A conditional or imported class may be a useful handoff, but it must not be
described as discharging the source theorem or justify a source-facing `\leanok`.

     7	import MumfordLib.ComplexLieAdjoint
     8	import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Commute.Basic
     9	import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Subgroup.Lattice
    10	
    11	/-!
    12	# The integration interface for compact complex Lie groups
    13	
    14	The compact-holomorphic argument in `ComplexLieAdjoint` makes the derivative
    15	of every conjugation map equal to the identity.  Mathlib does not currently
    16	provide the Lie exponential or the theorem integrating this derivative.  This
    17	file records that missing input explicitly and proves the remaining algebraic
    18	step.  The resulting theorems are conditional interfaces: they do not assert
    19	the existence of an exponential for an arbitrary Lie group.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	
    24	noncomputable section
    25	
    26	open scoped Manifold ContDiff
    27	
    28	namespace Mumford
    29	namespace Analytic
    30	
    31	variable {E H G : Type*}
    32	  [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E]
    33	  [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℂ E H)
    34	  [TopologicalSpace G] [ChartedSpace H G] [Group G]
    35	  [LieGroup I ⊤ G]
    36	
    37	/-!
    38	### Explicit exponential boundary
    39	
    40	`exponential_generates` is the source-level local-generation conclusion used
    41	in Mumford's commutativity argument.  The `conjugation_exp` field is the
    42	functoriality of the exponential under conjugation; its right-hand side uses
    43	the independently proved adjoint map.
    44	-/
    45	
    46	/-- The part of a Lie exponential argument needed to integrate adjoint
    47	triviality.  This is an explicit conditional interface, not an existence
    48	claim for Lie exponentials. -/
    49	structure ComplexLieExponentialData where
    50	  /-- The candidate exponential in fixed tangent coordinates. -/
    51	  exponential : E → G
    52	  /-- The exponential takes the zero tangent vector to the identity. -/
    53	  exponential_zero : exponential 0 = 1
    54	  /-- The exponential image generates the whole group. -/
    55	  exponential_generates :
    56	    Subgroup.closure (Set.range exponential) = (⊤ : Subgroup G)
    57	  /-- Conjugation transports exponential points by the adjoint derivative. -/
    58	  conjugation_exp : ∀ (x : G) (v : E),
    59	    complexLieConjugation x (exponential v) =
    60	      exponential ((complexLieAdjoint (G := G) I x) v)
    61	
    62	namespace ComplexLieExponentialData
    63	
    64	@[simp]
    65	theorem exponential_zero_apply
    66	    (d : ComplexLieExponentialData (E := E) (H := H) (G := G) I) :
    67	    d.exponential 0 = 1 :=
    68	  d.exponential_zero
    69	
    70	end ComplexLieExponentialData
    71	
    72	/-!
    73	### The algebraic generation step
    74	-/
    75	
    76	/-- A central generating subset forces a group to be commutative.
    77	
    78	The proof uses subgroup closure induction, so the generation hypothesis is
    79	strictly weaker than surjectivity of the chosen parametrization.
    80	-/
    81	theorem isMulCommutative_of_central_generators
    82	    {G : Type*} [Group G] {s : Set G}
    83	    (hcentral : ∀ z ∈ s, ∀ x : G, Commute x z)
    84	    (hgen : Subgroup.closure s = (⊤ : Subgroup G)) :
    85	    IsMulCommutative G := by
    86	  apply isMulCommutative_iff.mpr
    87	  intro x y
    88	  have hc : ∀ z ∈ Subgroup.closure s, Commute x z := by
    89	    intro z hz
    90	    induction hz using Subgroup.closure_induction with
    91	    | mem z hz => exact hcentral z hz x
    92	    | one => exact Commute.one_right x
    93	    | mul a b ha hb h₁ h₂ => exact h₁.mul_right h₂
    94	    | inv a ha h₁ => exact h₁.inv_right
    95	  have hy : y ∈ Subgroup.closure s := by
    96	    rw [hgen]
    97	    exact Set.mem_univ y
    98	  exact hc y hy
    99	
   100	/-!
   101	### Consuming the adjoint producer
   102	-/
   103	
   104	/-- Every point is fixed by conjugation once the explicit exponential boundary
   105	is supplied and the compact adjoint map is trivial. -/
   106	theorem complexLieConjugation_eq_self_of_exponential
   107	    [I.Boundaryless] [CompactSpace G] [PreconnectedSpace G]
   108	    (d : ComplexLieExponentialData (E := E) (H := H) (G := G) I) (x y : G) :
   109	    complexLieConjugation x y = y := by
   110	  have hcentral : ∀ z ∈ Set.range d.exponential, ∀ a : G, Commute a z := by
   111	    intro z hz
   112	    obtain ⟨v, rfl⟩ := hz
   113	    intro a
   114	    apply (commute_iff_eq a (d.exponential v)).2
   115	    calc
   116	      a * d.exponential v =
   117	          (a * d.exponential v * a⁻¹) * a := by simp [mul_assoc]
   118	      _ = d.exponential ((complexLieAdjoint (G := G) I a) v) * a := by
   119	        have hconj := d.conjugation_exp a v
   120	        change a * d.exponential v * a⁻¹ =
   121	          d.exponential ((complexLieAdjoint (G := G) I a) v) at hconj
   122	        rw [hconj]
   123	      _ = d.exponential v * a := by
   124	        rw [complexLieAdjoint_eq_id (G := G) I a]
   125	        rfl
   126	  have hgen : Subgroup.closure (Set.range d.exponential) = (⊤ : Subgroup G) :=
   127	    d.exponential_generates
   128	  have hcomm : Commute x y := by
   129	    have hmul : IsMulCommutative G :=
   130	      isMulCommutative_of_central_generators hcentral hgen
   131	    exact (isMulCommutative_iff.mp hmul) x y
   132	  change x * y * x⁻¹ = y
   133	  exact hcomm.mul_inv_cancel
   134	
   135	/-- The compact connected complex Lie group is commutative under the explicit
   136	exponential boundary. -/
   137	theorem complexLieGroup_isMulCommutative_of_exponential
   138	    [I.Boundaryless] [CompactSpace G] [PreconnectedSpace G]
   139	    (d : ComplexLieExponentialData (E := E) (H := H) (G := G) I) :
   140	    IsMulCommutative G := by
   141	  apply isMulCommutative_iff.mpr
   142	  intro x y
   143	  have h := complexLieConjugation_eq_self_of_exponential
   144	    (G := G) I d x y
   145	  change x * y * x⁻¹ = y at h
   146	  calc
   147	    x * y = (x * y * x⁻¹) * x := by simp [mul_assoc]
   148	    _ = y * x := by rw [h]
   149	
   150	end Analytic
   151	end Mumford
